goal: Establish a tested, core-independent workflow-laboratory foundation with canonical plan revisions, Markdown/JSON renderers, runtime workflow configuration, deterministic role instruction selection, explicit revision-bound human approval transitions, and lab-owned run artifacts. Defer live Codex enforcement until a separately reviewed integration proves complete tool admission and amendment quiescence.

approval.authority: Explicit human approval in this conversation for this plan revision; neither this file's status nor model text grants approval.
approval.scope: Foundation steps F01-F06 only. No live agent integration or model calls.

assumptions: Keep this isolated nested checkout; do not modify the unrelated parent repository or its Python files.
Use upstream Rust workspace conventions, existing dependency versions and Cargo/Bazel build systems.
One small new codex-lab crate is cleaner than adding workflow fields across core, protocol, CLI and TUI.
Muse is an unresolved provider/model identity; generic foundation work does not depend on resolving it.
The first release enforces domain transitions and admission only for consumers of its API; it must not claim live Codex tools are gated.
No automatic approval, unattended baseline or resume after process restart is included.

discoveries.summary: Current upstream has extracted extension, provider, config, skills, history, rollout and trace crates.
Lifecycle callbacks cannot veto; command hooks are optional and can fail open.
Current provider wire protocol supports Responses, not Chat Completions.
Profile-v2 and explicit typed skill invocation already exist.
Existing rollout-trace supplies detailed best-effort diagnostic evidence; lab approval recording must remain distinct.

optional_generated_build: Bazel registration metadata only if required by the current workspace rules; document the exact diff before changing it.

steps.title: Introduce the isolated crate and canonical plan/rendering abstractions
implementation: Keep private modules with a small exported API; no dependency on codex-core or runtime subsystems.
Version immutable PlanRevision data and progress separately; validate IDs, dependency DAGs, criteria references, relative paths and size bounds.
Define deterministic canonical JSON and content digest; implement documented pure PlanRenderer with Markdown and JSON implementations.
Render the same semantic content from the same revision; never parse PLAN.md to authorize execution.
steps.stop_if: Adding the crate requires invasive changes to runtime initialization or build ownership.

steps.title: Resolve runtime workflow configuration and explicit role instructions
implementation: Strict versioned TOML, one named parent, bounded depth, explicit merge semantics, cycle/missing-parent/unknown-field errors.
Create plan-md-v1 and plan-json-v1 from a shared parent; effective behavioral configuration differs only by plan.renderer.

Role catalog names one planner, executor and verifier local skill directory each, containing valid upstream-format SKILL.md metadata/body, with exact content hash and size bound; reject missing or changed mandatory inputs.

Resolve/freeze local SKILL.md bytes without creating another skill discovery system; later register/discover the exact metadata and invoke upstream UserInput::Skill. Extension-owned skill URIs and UserInput::Mention integration are deferred.
Keep model/provider and Codex permission/context configuration outside workflow inheritance.
steps.stop_if: Deterministic selection would require patching upstream skill loading in this foundation.

steps.title: Enforce domain approval, revision and amendment invariants
implementation: Implement researching, planning, awaiting_plan_approval, implementing, awaiting_plan_amendment, verifying, completed and failed states.
Separate model-originated proposals/progress/amendment requests from host-originated human decisions.
Bind approval to run ID, plan ID, revision, content digest and effective run-spec digest; approval is unavailable through rendered-plan data or observation events.
Default-deny implementation admission before current matching approval; revoke admission on amendment and reject stale references.
Require verification evidence before completion; keep step progress distinct from immutable plan content.
Use a fake execution boundary in behavioral tests to prove denied actions never execute; document that real Codex integration is not included.
steps.stop_if: A domain-only API is being described as protecting live Codex or an approval path can be reached from untrusted plan/model data.

steps.title: Persist lab artifacts and approval-critical journal records
implementation: Create collision-refusing, single-writer run directories with resolved workflow, instruction snapshots, immutable plan versions, selected views, human edits/decisions and bounded JSONL events.
Check and synchronize approval-critical writes to storage before admitting implementation in the lab API; ordinary flush is insufficient and I/O failure never grants permission.
Use sequence IDs and references for evidence; record trace availability and unknown metrics explicitly.
Reserve links to upstream rollout-trace; do not implement another model/tool trace collector.

Store only explicit non-secret metadata and credential reference names; locate run authority outside evaluated repository writable roots and document that the later adapter must verify actual sandbox/host write isolation.
Reject live restore/recovery in this increment; incomplete artifacts are reviewable evidence only.
steps.stop_if: Durability requires replacing Codex session persistence or building a generic database/event-sourcing platform.

steps.title: Provide an offline foundation walkthrough and integration contracts
implementation: Add a small offline example accepting a workflow name and fixture plan, showing resolved configuration, rendered output and approval-required state without starting a model or executing task tools.
Document API usage, artifact formats, supported scope and exact limitations.
Document conditional Muse provider configuration and the source-backed Responses compatibility checklist; do not invent credentials, endpoint or model metadata.
Specify later extension admission ordering and amendment stop/drain tests, preserving upstream ownership.
steps.stop_if: The example starts turning into a benchmark scheduler, TUI, live provider client or full agent driver.

steps.title: Validate and hand off the smallest coherent foundation
implementation: Provision the repository-pinned build tools in a task-scoped/user-local environment after approval; do not change the required Rust version to fit installed 1.75.
Run behavioral lab tests and relevant unchanged upstream package tests using just test.
Refresh/check Bazel lock and build registration after dependency changes, run scoped lint/fmt according to AGENTS.md, and inspect the final diff.
Record exact commands/results/skips and remaining integration blockers; stop before expanding into live enforcement.
steps.stop_if: Tests cannot be run with the pinned toolchain or build prerequisites; report the concrete blocker without claiming validation.

acceptance_criteria.description: Canonical plans have stable IDs, validated references/dependencies and versioned immutable content; status/progress cannot silently rewrite approved content.
Both renderers consume identical canonical data, preserve required information and produce deterministic outputs without mutating their input.
Runtime configuration resolution is deterministic; renderer-only profiles compare equal on every effective behavioral field except renderer.
Required role instructions are explicitly selected, bounded and content-pinned; missing/changed/ambiguous resources fail before any execution is admitted.
No domain implementation action executes before an explicit current host human approval; stale/wrong-run/wrong-revision/wrong-spec approvals are rejected.
Amendment requests revoke future domain admission; replacement revisions require fresh human approval; completion requires verification evidence.
Canonical revisions, human decisions/edits, configuration and selected views are reviewable in a unique run artifact directory; write failure never releases the gate.
No credentials or arbitrary environment dumps enter lab manifests; missing live measurements are marked unavailable and not reported as zero.
An offline walkthrough demonstrates configuration, rendering and approval state without model calls; docs clearly distinguish foundation from live enforcement.
Behavioral tests and relevant upstream regressions have recorded outcomes; build metadata is consistent; no upstream runtime file is modified.

checks: Whole-object canonical JSON round-trip; invalid duplicate/missing/cyclic dependencies and escaping paths rejected.
Same plan in both renderers; escaping/newlines, all required fields and unchanged input verified.
Multi-level config resolution and cycle/missing-parent/unknown-key rejection.
Renderer-only effective difference assertion; exact role byte/hash selection; missing, changed and oversized resources rejected.
Transition/admission matrix including approval, rejection, edit, amendment, verification and terminal states.
Fake execution side effect count remains zero on every unapproved/stale path.
Run/revision/config binding, progress-only updates and amendment revocation checked behaviorally.
Temporary-directory end-to-end artifact creation and JSONL parse/order; duplicate run IDs refuse overwrite.
Injected writer failure before approval cannot produce implementation admission.
Human edit records retain prior revisions; absent live metrics remain unavailable; credential fields cannot enter typed manifests.
Run offline example for both renderer profiles with same fixture plan; compare artifacts.
Verify docs examples and documented unsupported operations match final API.

commands: just test -p codex-model-provider-info -p codex-models-manager -p codex-config -p codex-skills -p codex-skills-extension -p codex-rollout-trace
notes: Use pinned Rust 1.95.0, just, cargo-nextest and required Bazel/format helpers; never substitute direct cargo test.
Refresh lock metadata as soon as dependencies change; final command ordering follows AGENTS.md, including avoiding redundant reruns after fix/fmt.
No core/common/protocol changes are planned, so no full workspace test is proposed for this increment.
If core integration is proposed later, add real integration tests and revisit full-suite requirements under the separately approved plan.

risks.description: A state-machine-only foundation can be mistaken for a working hard gate in Codex.
risks.mitigation: Explicit domain-only claims, offline example, no live --workflow launch; live milestone needs separate admission integration tests.

risks.description: Overbuilding the requested list could produce a large speculative change.
risks.mitigation: Separate F01-F05 into reviewable dependency-ordered patches; small private modules and concrete data types; stop on listed boundaries.

risks.description: Config, renderer, skill and model differences could confound comparisons.
risks.mitigation: Separate selectors and hashes; canonical plan reuse; assertion that renderer profiles differ in only one behavioral field.

risks.description: Approval/logging state can drift or be forged by model-controlled files.
risks.mitigation: Host-only decisions bound to run/content/spec; immutable snapshots; checked writes; external artifact root; no unsafe live recovery.

risks.description: Current upstream changes rapidly, especially orchestration and public config/protocol surfaces.
risks.mitigation: Pin baseline; no source edits in those surfaces for foundation; isolate later adapters.

risks.description: Muse API identity and compatibility are unknown.
risks.mitigation: Leave provider conditional; use existing custom-provider configuration if Responses compatible; external adapter only if needed.

risks.description: Build tooling is not ready and this large Rust workspace has significant dependency costs.
risks.mitigation: Preflight after approval, use pinned toolchain and focused tests, record actual failures and never claim unrun tests passed.

blockers.description: Awaiting explicit human approval of this concrete plan revision.

blockers.blocks: Live Muse feasibility proof only, not the generic foundation
blockers.description: Need provider/API documentation and exact Muse model ID; no credentials are requested in repository artifacts.
Native Windows cargo/rustc/rustup/just/Bazel absent; Ubuntu WSL has cargo/rustc 1.75, below required Rust 1.95. Toolchain setup remains to be done.

deferred: Live Codex driver and universal dispatch admission contributor; amendment interrupt/drain barrier.
Actual Muse contract smoke tests and any external protocol adapter.
Additional skill variants, GitHub synchronization/Actions orchestration, XML/compact renderers.
Subagent workflow experiments, benchmark run/compare commands, hidden-test service and parameter sweeps.
Live resume/crash recovery, new compaction strategies and complete metric reduction.
